ex: Nyngkong, plie ïa ka app. Hadien kata, log in.
Ka sha ne ka kophi?
n: ne is the everyday 'or'; lane is a little more formal.

ex: Ha kaba kut, ngi la poi ha ka hotel.
Hadien kata, kylla sha kti mon ha ka bank.
n: kylla is turn; kti mon is right.

ex: Nga don kam mynta. Nga lah ban phone ïa phi hadien?
n: sa before the verb also means 'later': ngan sa phone.

ex: Ka rel ka la wan lait. Namarkata, ngam shym la poi ha ka meeting jong nga.
Ngi la peit ka phlim. Hadien kata, ngi la bam ja janmiet.
Nga donkam ka kpu bad ruh khyndiat ka dud.
n: kpu is bread; ruh after bad adds 'as well'.

ex: Nga kwah ban mih, hynrei hadien kata ka la sdang ban slap.
n: sdang is begin; ka is the dummy subject for weather.

ex: To ngi leit sha ka duriaw. Ne lehse sha ka park?
Ha kaba sdang, ka ktien English ka la eh shibun ïa nga.
n: eh is hard, difficult; sdang is begin.

ex: Kumno kumno ruh, kumno ka la long ka weekend jong me?
n: Informal: me to a male friend, pha to a female.

ex: Ha kawei ka sngi, nga kwah ban leit sha Japan.
n: Literally 'on one day'; works for past stories and future wishes. Less certain it is idiomatic rather than calqued.

ex: Kynsan hi, ka bijli ka la lut.
n: Uncertain word: kynsan for 'suddenly' needs a speaker's check. bijli (electricity) is the Shillong word for power.

ex: Nga la jah ïa ka wallet jong nga, hynrei ka bha ba uwei u briew u la shem.
n: No single 'luckily': 'but it's good that' does the job.

ex: Nga khie ha hynñiew baje man ka sngi.
n: man ka sngi is 'every day'.

ex: Nga ju khie ha hynriew baje.
n: khie covers both wake up and get up; ju marks the habit (usually).

ex: Nga bam ja mynstep ha ïing.
n: ja is cooked rice and stands for a meal; jingbam mynstep is the noun 'breakfast'.

ex: To ngi bam ja ha ka sngi lang.
n: Less certain of a fixed word for lunch; 'eat at midday' is a safe rendering. lang is together.

ex: Ngi bam ja janmiet ha hynñiew baje.
n: janmiet is evening.

ex: Nga sum man ka sngi mynstep.
n: sum is bathe; it covers shower too.

ex: Sait bniat shwa ban leit thiah.
n: sait is wash; bniat is teeth.

ex: Nga kup jain bad nga bam ja mynstep.
n: kup (wrap, put on) plus jain (clothes) is my best guess; check with a speaker.

ex: Nga leit thiah ha khadwei baje.
n: khadwei is eleven.

ex: Nga leit sha kam da ka bas.
n: da is 'by' for the means.

ex: Nga thait. Nga kwah ban leit sha ïing.
n: phai sha ïing (turn back home) is also common.

ex: Nga poi ha ïing ha hynriew baje.
n: poi is arrive.

ex: To ngi leit sha ïew ha ka sngi Saturday.
n: ïew is market; thied (buy) names the actual shopping.

ex: Nga peit TV janmiet.
Nga sngap jingrwai ha ka bas.
n: sngap is listen; jingrwai is song, music.

ex: Nga trei ïa ka homework jong nga hadien ka skul.
n: homework and skul are loans every student uses.

ex: Nga shet ja janmiet man ka miet.
n: shet is cook.

ex: To ngi leit kai ha ka park.
n: kai is stroll, go out for pleasure.

ex: Nga lehkai football man ka sngi Saturday.
n: lehkai is play for games and sports; sport names stay in English.

ex: Nga leit sha ïew man ka sngi Monday.
Nga sait jain ha ka sngi Sunday.
n: sait jain is literally 'wash clothes'.

ex: Ngi pynkhuid ïa ka ïing man ka sngi Saturday.
n: pyn- plus khuid (clean) is 'make clean'.

ex: Sait kti shwa ban bam ja janmiet.
Ngan shet kophi. Phi kwah?
n: shet (cook) is used for making tea and coffee.

ex: Nga leit sha skul da ka bas.
Kiew ha ka bas hangne bad hiar ha ka park.
n: kiew is climb, get on; hiar is get off.

ex: Hiar na ka bas ha ka stop ba bud.
n: ba bud (the following) for 'next' is my best guess.

ex: Hangno nga lah ban thied tiket?
Ngi kwah ban shim ka kali ha kiraya na ka bynta lai sngi.
n: kiraya (hire) is the Shillong loan; less certain of a pure Khasi word.

ex: Sumar haba phi lait ïa ka lynti.
n: lait (pass over) for crossing is my best guess; sumar is 'be careful'.

ex: Kylla sha kti diang ha ka bank.
n: kti diang is left; kti mon is right.

ex: Nga lah ban shim dur?
n: dur is picture, photo.

ex: Nga thngan. To ngi bam.
n: thngan is a verb: no 'be' needed.

ex: Nga kwah ban dih um. Don um hangne?
n: Uncertain of the adjective (sliang?); 'I want to drink water' is the safe way.

ex: Nga thait. Ngan leit thiah.
Kloi, ngin poi lait!
n: kloi is hurry.

ex: Ka rel ka poi ha ka por mynta.
n: ha ka por is 'on time'.

ex: Ngi la sngewtynnad shibun ha ka duriaw.
n: sngewtynnad is enjoy, have fun.

ex: Ka khlieh jong nga ka pang. Phi don ka dawai?
n: khlieh is head, dawai is medicine.

ex: U khun jong nga u pang shit.
n: Uncertain: pang shit (sick-hot) for fever; many simply say fever.

ex: Dih kane ka dawai ar sien ha ka sngi.
n: Khasi drinks medicine (dih), even tablets. sien is 'times'.

ex: Nga donkam ban phone ïa uwei u briew.
n: phone is a verb as it stands.

ex: Ngan sa phah message ïa phi hadien.
n: phah is send.

ex: Nga lah ban charge ïa ka phone jong nga hangne?
Nga dang nang ka ktien English na ka bynta ka kam jong nga.
n: nang is learn and know how; pule (study) is the school word.

t: Ka kyrteng jong nga ka long [name]
ex: Khublei, ka kyrteng jong nga ka long Carlos.
Nga wan na Mexico.
Nga shong ha Chicago.
Nga laiphew snem.
n: Less certain: Ka rta jong nga ka long [number] snem is the fuller form.

ex: Nga dei ka nonghikai.
n: u for a man, ka for a woman; nong- makes the job noun.

t: Kane ka dei ka [person] jong nga / Une u dei u [person] jong nga
ex: Kane ka dei ka tnga jong nga, ka Julia.
n: kane for a woman, une for a man. tnga is spouse.

ex: Map, phi kren ka ktien English?

Nga dang nang ka ktien English ha ka skul janmiet.
n: dang marks the ongoing learning.

ex: Kumno ban ong 'Danke' ha ka ktien English?
Aiu ka mut jong 'busy'?
n: mut is meaning.

ex: Ngam sngewthuh ïa kane ka ktien.
Ka long lai baje.
n: ka is the dummy subject; baje is o'clock.

t: Ka sngi kha jong nga ka long ka [date]
ex: Ka sngi kha jong nga ka long ka lai tarik u bnai Mei.
n: tarik (date) is the everyday loan; months take u bnai.

ex: Lano ka sngi kha jong phi?
Katno baje ka phlim?
Katno baje ka plie ka bank?
n: plie is open; the place's marker is echoed before the verb.

ex: Katno kane ka T-shirt?
Ka long khadar tyngka, sngewbha.
n: tyngka is rupees, money.

ex: Nga lah ban siew da ka card?
n: siew is pay; da is 'by'.

ex: Phi don ka dud?
Ka heh palat khyndiat. Phi don kaba kham rit?
n: palat is 'too much'; kham rit is 'smaller'.

ex: Ai ïa nga ka kophi kawei, sngewbha.
n: Literally 'give me'; sngewbha makes it polite, not rude.

ex: Nga kwah ka sandwich kawei, sngewbha.
Ngan shim ka dohkha, sngewbha.
n: dohkha is fish.

ex: Ai ïa nga shi glass um, sngewbha.
n: glass is the loan; shi is 'one'.

ex: Phi kwah biang khyndiat ka ja?
n: biang (again, more) plus khyndiat does 'some more'.

ex: Phi kwah ban wan sha ka party jong nga?
Hangno ka steshon rel?

n: jan is near; tam after an adjective makes the superlative.

ex: Kylla sha kti diang ha ka balang.
n: balang is church.

ex: Ka bank ka don sha kti diang.
n: kti diang is left, kti mon is right.

ex: Ka dukan kpu ka don ryngkat ka bank.
n: ryngkat (beside) is my best guess; hajan (near) is safe.

ex: Shi tiket sha Guwahati, sngewbha.

t: Kaei ka bas kaba leit sha [place]?

n: kaei is 'which, what' before a noun.

ex: Lano ka rel ba bud sha Leeds?
n: ba bud (the following) for 'next' is my best guess.

t: Phi lah ban wallam ïa nga sha [place]?
ex: Phi lah ban wallam ïa nga sha ka airport, sngewbha?
n: wallam is bring, take along.

ex: Ka shim kumba arphew minit da ka bas.
n: kumba before a number is 'about'.

t: Nga kwah ka kamra na ka bynta [number] miet
ex: Nga kwah ka kamra kawei na ka bynta ar miet, sngewbha.

n: kam is ka plus ym (not); the thing's marker changes it: um for u.
